itinerary.cal: Most parties do it as one long push from the Stuart Lake trailhead. Camping at Colchuck Lake between May 15 and Oct. 31 needs an Enchantments overnight permit from Recreation.gov; a day trip does not.
itinerary.totalNote: One very long day from the car: hike past Colchuck Lake toward Aasgard Pass and climb the headwall cracks. From the top, either rappel the route or carry on up the Northeast Buttress to the summit and come down to Aasgard Pass. A party that went to the summit took about 16.5 hours car to car.

days.title: Colchuck Lake, Dragons of Eden and out
days.objective: Climb the headwall and return to the Stuart Lake trailhead
days.note: Hike the Stuart Lake trail and branch left to Colchuck Lake (about 8 miles round trip to the lake itself). Leave the trail on the climb toward Aasgard Pass and stash packs below the face, roughly three hours from the car. A short fifth-class slab reaches the first pitch. There are two ways down. You can rappel from the headwall belay with two 60 m ropes. Or you can continue up the long ramp and easy fifth-class ground of the Northeast Buttress to the 8,842 ft summit, rappel the descent gully, scramble loose ground down to Aasgard Pass, and walk back past the lake.

schedule.label: Leave the Stuart Lake trailhead
schedule.detail: Headlamp start.

schedule.label: Leave the Aasgard Pass trail
schedule.detail: About three hours from the car. Drop packs and walk 15 minutes to the base.

schedule.label: Top of the headwall
schedule.detail: The cracks took close to five hours. Rappel from here with two 60 m ropes, or keep going.

schedule.label: Summit via the Northeast Buttress
schedule.detail: A bit over an hour of easier climbing above the headwall.

schedule.label: Back at the packs
schedule.detail: A rappel and loose scrambling down to Aasgard Pass, then back to the stash.

schedule.label: Back at the car
schedule.detail: Close to three hours out past Colchuck Lake.

itinerary.totalNote: A single day from the Stuart Lake trailhead: approach past Colchuck Lake toward Aasgard Pass, climb six pitches, rappel the neighbouring Dragons of Eden line and hike out. No source gives a car-to-car time. The approach alone takes three to four hours.

days.title: Colchuck Lake, Dragon's Jaw and out
days.objective: Climb the six pitches, rappel and return to the trailhead
days.note: Hike the Stuart Lake trail and branch left to Colchuck Lake (about 8 miles round trip to the lake alone), then head up toward Aasgard Pass. Cross the stream roughly 100 ft below the first cliffs and aim for the scree hill right of the mossy stream beds to reach this northeast-most buttress. Plan on three to four hours from the car. Six pitches of 5.9+ to 5.11- crack climbing share a top-out with Dragons of Eden. Rappel that route with two 60 m ropes, or carry on up the Northeast Buttress to the summit and descend to Aasgard Pass.

itinerary.totalNote: A single day from the Stuart Lake trailhead: walk in past Colchuck Lake to the glacier toe, climb five hard pitches, rappel the line and walk out. No source gives an approach or car-to-car time.

days.title: Colchuck Lake, New Dark Ages and out
days.objective: Climb five pitches above the Colchuck Glacier toe and return
days.note: Hike the Stuart Lake trail and branch left to Colchuck Lake (about 8 miles round trip to the lake alone). Continue around the lake and up talus to the wall above the toe of the Colchuck Glacier, right of the Boving-Christensen line. There are five pitches from 5.10+ to 5.11+, and the first two link on a 60 m rope unless the snow sits unusually low. To descend, walk the top ledge south to its high point and find a two-bolt anchor before the corner. From there it takes about four double-rope rappels down the route. The alternative is roughly 1,500 ft of fourth and low fifth class to the summit of Dragontail.

days.note: Hike the Stuart Lake trail and branch left to Colchuck Lake (about 8 miles round trip to the lake alone). Dragonfruit starts just right of New Dark Ages, with five pitches of 5.10- to 5.11, and the third is the standout. Come down the New Dark Ages rappels (about four double-rope raps from a two-bolt anchor on the top ledge), or keep climbing to the summit of Dragontail.

itinerary.cal: Summer to early fall, once the trail over Ingalls Pass is clear of snow.
itinerary.totalNote: A day trip: hike over Ingalls Pass to Ingalls Lake, scramble the East Ridge approach gully to the notch between the North and East peaks, climb two short pitches, rappel and hike out. No source gives a car-to-car time for this route.

days.title: Ingalls Lake and the East Peak
days.objective: Climb the Southwest Face of the East Peak and return
days.note: From the Esmeralda trailhead, climb about 3 miles to Ingalls Pass and drop about a mile to Ingalls Lake (about 9 miles and 2,500 ft round trip for the lake alone). From the lake, go up the approach gully used for the East Ridge and scramble to the chockstone in the notch between the North and East peaks, where the route begins. The two easy pitches pass three rappel stations. Rappel the line, going past the chockstone on the last one to get back to the left side of the gully. Some parties carry on up the East Ridge of the North Peak.

itinerary.cal: Summer to early fall, once the trail over Ingalls Pass is clear of snow.
itinerary.totalNote: A day trip: hike over Ingalls Pass to Ingalls Lake, approach the southeast face as for its neighbour Friends in High Places, climb two pitches up the left-side dihedral and rappel. No source gives a car-to-car time for this route.

days.title: Ingalls Lake and Ingalls Error
days.objective: Climb the two southeast-face pitches and return
days.note: From the Esmeralda trailhead, climb about 3 miles to Ingalls Pass and drop about a mile to Ingalls Lake (about 9 miles and 2,500 ft round trip for the lake alone). Approach the southeast face as for Friends in High Places and start at the base of the right-facing dihedral on the far left. Belay well left to stay out of rockfall. The two pitches, the second a runout 5.7, finish at the top of the face with no fixed anchor, so bring cord to sling a large knob and rappel. There is also a rappel station on the right flank of the face.
